{{Short description|German chemist (born 1967)}}
'''Uwe Meierhenrich''' (born 23 October 1967 in [[Detmold]]) is a German Physico-Chemist. He is a professor of [[Analytical Chemistry|Analytical]] and [[Physical Chemistry]] at the [[University of Nice Sophia Antipolis]] in [[France]].

== Academic life ==
Meierhenrich was raised in a family of teachers and professors. He studied [[chemistry]] at the [[Philipps-University Marburg]] and obtained a Ph.D. degree in [[physical chemistry]] at the [[University of Bremen]] by Thiemann. He did postdoctoral work at the [[Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research]] in Katlenburg-Lindau and at the French [[Synchrotron]] Center [[Laboratoire pour l'utilisation du rayonnement électromagnétique|LURE]]. In 2003 he earned his [[habilitation]] with the publication of ''The Origin of Biomolecular Asymmetry'' at the [[University of Bremen]]. In 2005 he was hired as a professor at the [[University of Nice Sophia Antipolis]] in [[France]]. For his work on [[chirality (chemistry)|chirality]], he was awarded the Horst-Pracejus-Prize of the [[Gesellschaft Deutscher Chemiker]] (German Chemical Society) in 2011.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Beyer|first1=Sonja|title=Gesellschaft Deutscher Chemiker verleiht Horst-Pracejus-Preis und Carl-Duisberg-Gedächtnispreis|date=18 March 2011 |language=German|trans-title=Gesellschaft Deutscher Chemiker awards Horst Pracejus Prize and Carl Duisberg Memorial Prize |
url=https://www.process.vogel.de/gesellschaft-deutscher-chemiker-verleiht-horst-pracejus-preis-und-carl-duisberg-gedaechtnispreis-a-307803/|website=Process|publisher=Vogel Business Media|access-date=6 May 2018}}</ref>

== Career ==
Meierhenrich was hired by the [[European Space Agency]] to develop instrumentation for its [[Rosetta (spacecraft)|Rosetta mission]] to [[67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko]]. The purpose of the instrumentation was to detect organic compounds on the comet's surface. To test it on Earth, he worked with scientists at [[Leiden University]] in the Netherlands who were making artificial cometary ice. They replicated the conditions in space, creating a cold vacuum and bombarding the ice with [[ultraviolet]] light. They succeeded in synthesizing 16 [[amino acids]]. When the Rosetta spacecraft reached 67P in 2014, it detected similar organic compounds in the comet. In further experiments at his lab in Nice, he analyzed cometary ice analogs with multidimensional gas chromatography and detected [[ribose]], one of the sugars that make up DNA.<ref name=Keats>{{cite news|last1=Keats|first1=Jonathon|title=Cooking Up Early-Earth Conditions|url=http://discovermagazine.com/2016/nov/brewing-life|access-date=6 May 2018|work=Discover Magazine|date=6 October 2016}}</ref>

Further experiments at the French [[Soleil (synchrotron)|SOLEIL synchrotron]] showed that [[life]]'s [[homochirality]] can also originate under [[interstellar space|interstellar]] conditions.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Cohen|first1=Philip|title=Life's building blocks created in space simulator|url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/dn2100-lifes-building-blocks-created-in-space-simulator/|access-date=6 May 2018|work=New Scientist|agency=New Scientist|date=27 March 2002}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Whitehouse|first1=David|title=Life's origins among the stars|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/science/nature/1897186.stm|access-date=6 May 2018|work=BBC News|date=27 March 2002}}</ref>
